Record and print a check

Source: R/checks.R
check_result.Rd

Prints [OK] or [FAIL] followed by a description, and records the result so that check_summary() can report how many checks passed. Use it to write your own checks while exploring a design or an analysis.

Usage

check_result(what, ok, section = NULL, note = FALSE)

Arguments

what

Description of the check, e.g. "every entry planted once".

ok

Logical. TRUE when the check passes; anything else (including NA) counts as a failure.

section

Optional label for grouping checks, e.g. "p-rep". Defaults to the label set with check_section().

note

Logical. If TRUE, the check is informational: it prints [NOTE] instead of [FAIL] when ok is not TRUE and is not counted as a failure.

Value

Invisibly, TRUE if the check passed.

See also

check_section(), check_summary(), check_reset(), check_design()

Examples

check_reset()
#> Ready to start: no earlier checks to clear. The checks you run from now on will be counted together.
check_result("two plus two is four", 2 + 2 == 4)
#>   [OK]   two plus two is four
check_result("a deliberate failure", FALSE, section = "demo")
#>   [FAIL] a deliberate failure
check_summary()
#> 
#> 1 of 2 checks passed
#> 
#> By section:
#>  section      checks passed failed notes
#>  (no section) 1      1      0      0    
#>  demo         1      0      1      0    
#> 
#> Failed checks (not correct):
#>  section check               
#>  demo    a deliberate failure
check_reset()
#> Earlier checks cleared (2 checks: 1 passed, 1 failed). Ready to start new checks.
